crime_highlights: Mr. Johnny and Mr. Scotchman each had knives.
Mr. Johnny had knives in both hands as he punched Mr. Lepretre.
He laid on Mr. Lepretre and stabbed him in the neck.
There were eight significant stab wounds including an 11.5 centimetre deep stab to the chest.
Mr. Lepretre died from the blood loss caused by the stabbing to his neck.
rationale_highlights: His family endured three generations of residential school abuse.
I have taken into account the context as explained in the Gladue report.
In considering all of the factors, and the Gladue considerations, a fit and proper sentence is life imprisonment without eligibility for parole for 14 years.

crime_highlights: Ms. Tom's injuries were consistent with having been punched, kicked, choked, and dragged along the ground.
The spinal injury would have been immediately fatal
at least four were delivered to her head, several blows were delivered to her face
Mr. George punched and/or kicked Ms. Tom at a minimum of eight to ten times during the course of the confrontation outside the house
rationale_highlights: I take judicial notice of the systemic and background factors that affect First Nations persons in Canada, including lingering institutional racism and historical effects of past policies and injustice.
I consider that the systemic difficulties and social and economic deprivation within the First Nations community has played a role in bringing Mr. George before this court.
I consider that there should be a significant emphasis on restorative justice in accordance with the Gladue principles
note: Effect is on restorative emphasis, not culpability; violence kept denunciation primary.

crime_highlights: the offender told his son to walk home and to take a black man-purse and a purple bag with him
They found what they believed to be cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and benzylpiperazine.
After being arrested, the offender also told the police that there were two guns in the purple bag.
They are both prohibited firearms and include: (1) an Aktak Arms Zoraki 9 mm semi-automatic pistol, loaded with three live rounds in a clip
rationale_highlights: Those circumstances, I conclude, mean that her moral blameworthiness is reduced.
she has faced the challenges that are faced by many First Nations Canadians: poverty, loss of cultural identity, victimization and family fragmentation
the offender's exceptional circumstances persuade me that the principles of sentencing can be met with a suspended sentence
the unique systemic factors in this case reduce the offender's moral culpability
note: No victim harm in the offence facts.
